SharedFlowBundle.name: ISAM-Common-CallISAM
SharedFlowBundle.Description:
Reusable building block: POSTs a pre-built request body to a primary ISAM host, failing over to a secondary host on transport failure or HTTP 500; exactly the "call itself to the ISAM endpoint is the same" part shared by every SAML/JWT type. Every other type-specific shared flow (ISAM-SAML-Light, ISAM-SAML-User, ISAM-SAML-TP, ISAM-SAML-Technical, ISAM-JWT-SAML, ISAM-JWT-Token) calls this one via FlowCallout instead of duplicating the failover logic.
INPUT variables (set these before the FlowCallout): isamcall.request.body string; the request payload to POST isamcall.request.contentType string; e.g. "application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8" or "application/json" isamcall.target.url.primary string; full URL of the primary ISAM host isamcall.target.url.secondary string; full URL of the secondary ISAM host isamcall.connectTimeoutMs string, optional (default: Apigee ServiceCallout default if unresolved) isamcall.ioTimeoutMs string, optional
OUTPUT variables (read these after the FlowCallout returns): isamcall.response.body string; whichever host actually responded isamcall.response.statusCode string; that host's HTTP status
This flow raises its own fault (RF-ISAM-Unavailable, HTTP 502) if both hosts failed or 500'd; the caller never sees that case as a normal return. Any other status (200, 400, other 5xx) returns normally with isamcall.response.statusCode set accordingly; it's the caller's job to decide what a non-200 response means for its own response shape.
